records.specification_basis: Lotus specifies a Hewland FG five-speed. The car-specific source identifies the Hewland FG; Hewland's construction manual identifies its face-dog clutch rings and selector hardware. The five-speed manual racing box is operated by the visible driver gear lever rather than paddles; the gate itself is not legible enough to establish the exact pattern. An H-pattern driver-shifted racing gearbox requires declutching to pull away from rest under the project's derivation. A Hewland face-dog racing gearbox is driven with clutchless running upshifts; the clutch remains a launch control. Hewland's dog-engagement technique requires removing engine driving load during the change; this is the supported throttle-lift technique, not a simulator observation. The period manual FG installation has no documented electronic cut system; the reviewed sources describe mechanical driver unloading instead. Manual blip is a downshift action in this model. Automatic blip is not an upshift action for this gearbox. The dogbox construction permits the authentic running downshift without clutch operation when the driver matches the shaft speed. Throttle lift is modeled for upshift unloading, not as a downshift field here. No downshift cut action is documented for the mechanical FG installation. A dogbox does not synchronize engine speed; the driver must match revs for a clean running downshift. The period mechanical installation has no documented automatic blip system. The inspected 72/D7 cockpit photos show a conventional continuous round rim. The wheel has no readout; instruments are separate analog gauges. No wheel-mounted shift-light strip or lamps are visible. The photographed rim is a closed circular wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern.
